title: 1.1.3 SDLC Writeup
description: Describe the five SDLC phases in your own words, then walk a real app through all five. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Describe the software development life-cycle (SDLC) in your own words.

Part 1 — Describe the phases. For each of the five phases below, write 1–2 sentences explaining what happens during that phase and why it matters:
1. Design (Planning & Requirements) — figuring out what to build and how it should work
2. Development (Coding) — writing the actual code that makes the software work
3. Testing — checking that the software works correctly and fixing bugs
4. Deployment — releasing the software so users can access it
5. Maintenance — updating, fixing, and improving the software after release

Part 2 — Real-world example. Choose one software product you actually use (Instagram, Spotify, Google Maps, Roblox, YouTube, Google Docs, etc.) and walk through how you think it went through each of the five phases. Best-guess reasoning is fine — no research required. Name the product and address all five phases.

Use your own words throughout. Do not copy definitions from the internet.

rubric.title: All five SDLC phases described
rubric.description: Student addresses all five phases (design, development, testing, deployment, maintenance) in Part 1. Each phase must be mentioned by name (or a clear synonym) and given at least one sentence of explanation. Credit requires all five to be present — partial coverage of 3–4 phases does not earn this criterion.

rubric.title: Phase descriptions are in own words
rubric.description: The phase descriptions read as the student's own understanding, not copied text from a website or textbook. Look for personal phrasing, natural variation in sentence structure, and plausible beginner-level explanations. Deny if the text matches dictionary-style definitions verbatim or reads as clearly copied from a source.

rubric.title: Specific software product named in Part 2
rubric.description: Student names a specific, real software product by name (e.g., Instagram, Spotify, Roblox — not just 'an app' or 'a website'). The product must be named clearly in the response. Generic references like 'some app I use' do not earn this criterion.

rubric.title: Real-world example walks through all five phases
rubric.description: Student applies all five SDLC phases to the chosen product in Part 2. Each phase must be addressed — either by name or clearly implied in sequence. Covering only 3 or 4 phases does not earn this criterion. Best-guess reasoning is acceptable; factual accuracy is not required as long as the reasoning is plausible.

rubric.title: Response is clear and organized
rubric.description: The response uses headings or numbered structure so phases are identifiable and is easy to read. Deny this criterion only for significant issues: no discernible structure, or writing that makes it impossible to evaluate the content. Do not deny for length — a short response that clearly covers the content is fine.
